concerns.message: Acceptance 1 requires the turning circle to stay within ±25 % of today's by rescaling `shipTuning`, but the turn rate can't be rescaled. `turnRate` is an integer number of heading units per world step (`step.ts:59`), and 1 is already the minimum. `HEADING_COUNT` = 64 is fixed by the 17-entry cosine table in `packages/simulation/src/heading.ts`, which this lane doesn't own, and by `PLACEMENT_HEADING_COUNT`. So a full turn always takes 64 steps, 3.2 s. At 5 tiles/s the turning radius is about 2.55 tiles. At 38–39 sub-units per step (≈3 tiles/s) it is about 1.5 tiles, which is −41 %. On screen, at 24 px against today's 16 px, the change is only about −12 % (≈41 px → ≈36 px).
concerns.consequence: The worker has three bad options. It can invent a turn-skipping or fractional-heading mechanic in `step.ts`/`state.ts`: that is a new ShipState field, turning slows to 4.8–6.4 s per full turn (less generous, not more), and it risks changing snapshot shapes. It can ship a unit test that quietly misses item 1. Or it can stop as blocked. Before workers start, settle that the turning circle is measured on screen (px) or as time per full turn, and that `turnRate` stays 1.

concerns.message: 3 tiles a second can't be represented exactly: 3 × 256 / 20 = 38.4 sub-units per world step, and `maxSpeed` must be an integer. 38 gives 2.97 tiles/s, which is 71.25 px/s at 24 px, just under the 72–80 band. 39 gives 3.05 tiles/s (73.1 px/s), and neighbouring docks then need to be ≥ 61 tiles apart by sea. Changing `SUB_UNITS_PER_TILE` to make it exact would break `packages/simulation/src/claim/claim.test.ts:67`, which hard-codes `* 256`. That file belongs to the parallel claim lane, which this lane may not touch.
concerns.consequence: A test that asserts a literal 3 tiles/s fails, or a worker changes the tile's sub-units and breaks the other lane's unit check at merge. Keep `SUB_UNITS_PER_TILE` at 256, pick 38 or 39, and assert against the constant.

concerns.message: The 20 s minimum between neighbours at ≈3 tiles/s means ≈60 tiles of sea path dock to dock. In a 112-tile map, that pushes the four islands back toward the corners, or puts their docks on the sides facing away from each other. The spawn slots must also stay outside the islands' bounding box. The only test of density is the new distance-to-obstacle rule. Nothing checks the plan's claim that routes are funnelled so ships on different routes pass within sight of each other.
concerns.consequence: The map can pass every validator and still look like today's layout at half size, with scattered shoal specks as filler. That fails the operator's "ships meet" intent without failing any check.

concerns.message: The no-empty-stretch validator doesn't say which distance it uses or how it treats the map edge. Chebyshev or octile distance at 10 would let tiles up to about 14 tiles (Euclidean) from any obstacle pass. The plan also doesn't say whether the map edge counts as non-sea.
concerns.consequence: The validator could pass open water that is outside the sight radius, which defeats item 3. Specify an integer squared-Euclidean distance to the nearest land, shoal, dock or rock tile, with the edge not counting.

concerns.message: The `out-of-sight` test places ships 16 tiles apart so they are "out of sight, but on each other's screen". At 24 px that is 384 px, and the view's half-width is 400 px. If the camera is clamped near the edge of a 112-tile map, the other ship is off the canvas.
concerns.consequence: The check that nothing of the other ship's colour is drawn passes without testing anything, because the ship is off-canvas. That weakens the visibility-boundary browser proof without anyone noticing. Use about 12–13 tiles apart, on a row where the camera isn't clamped.

concerns.message: "Brake until the dock hint reads Press E": holding ArrowDown once the ship has stopped makes it reverse (`nextSpeed` reverses from a stop). The hint only reads "Press E" when the ship is within the 1.5-tile reach and at or below `dockMaxSpeed`. Tapping E itself is safe, because `InputGate` latches taps until the next world step.
concerns.consequence: If the ship stops short of the reach, the test backs away and times out, which is a new source of flakiness in the 5-repeat run. Stop a few tiles off the dock, creep in with short throttle taps, release every key as soon as the hint reads "Press E", then tap E.

simpler_alternative: Keep `SUB_UNITS_PER_TILE` (256), `HEADING_COUNT` (64) and `turnRate` (1) unchanged. Rescale only `maxSpeed` (38 or 39), acceleration (2 or 3), braking (3), drag (1) and the dock speed and reach. Define handling feel in on-screen terms, which the 24 px scale was chosen to preserve: time to full speed, stopping distance in tiles, and the turning circle in pixels or time per turn. That needs no change to the `step.ts` mechanics and doesn't touch the claim lane's constants. For the map, write a small script under `assets/source/maps` that produces the `.tmj` from a symmetric sketch, then run the existing `map:build` and validators. Iterating on the layout is then quick, and there are no ~50 hand-placed shoal clumps in Tiled.
cheap_experiment: In a scratch vitest (about 15 minutes), run `sail()` on an open synthetic map with candidate tuning {maxSpeed 38 and 39, acceleration 2 and 3, braking 3, drag 1, turnRate 1}. Measure the steps to full speed, the braking distance in tiles, and the turning-circle diameter in tiles and in pixels at 24 px, and compare each with today's tuning. If the turning circle in tiles falls outside ±25 % with turnRate 1 (expected: about −41 %) while the on-screen value stays within about −12 %, the turning-circle wording has to be settled before any worker starts.
